explanation: In Thailand the feet are considered the lowest and dirtiest part of the body, so sitting with legs crossed in a way that shows the soles of your feet toward others is considered extremely impolite. In a business setting, a tucked or closed leg position is safer, and shaking your foot or leg while seated is not rude but makes you look unprofessional.
local_tip: Keep both feet flat on the floor or tuck them discreetly to the side so your soles never face a colleague or client.

also_check.note: Crossing legs at the ankle is common, but sitting with an ankle on the knee or showing soles can read as casual or disrespectful in formal meetings.
Crossing legs is common among men, but exposing the sole of your shoe toward a senior person is frowned upon.
Showing the soles of your feet, including by crossing legs, is offensive in Gulf business settings.
